cards.explanation: The answer is how this wicked thing happened. Their question, word for word, is "Tell us, how did this wicked thing happen?" (Judges 20:3) I think they want the account from someone who was there. And that's who steps up next, the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman.

The answer is True. The Levite says the men of Gibeah rose up against him in the night, surrounded the house and intended to kill him. Then he says they abused his concubine and she died. This is a heavy part of the story, friends, and I think it hurts to read.

The answer is that Gibeah's men did a disgraceful act in Israel. The Levite says he sent her throughout the land "…because they had committed a lewd and disgraceful act in Israel." (Judges 20:6) He points the whole nation at what Gibeah's men did.

The answer is that not one of them will go home. They say it together: "Not one of us will return to his tent or to his house." (Judges 20:8) That's a big promise from the crowd gathered at Mizpah. Nobody is slipping out the back.

The answer is provisions, the supplies an army needs while it marches. They take ten men out of every hundred, a hundred out of every thousand and a thousand out of every ten thousand to supply them (Judges 20:10). No bakery runs on good intentions, friends. You need supplies, and so does an army.

The answer is death. Israel asks Benjamin to hand over the wicked men of Gibeah "…so we can put them to death and purge Israel of this evil." (Judges 20:13) It's a serious demand, and it comes before any fighting starts.

The answer is False. The text says, "But the Benjamites refused to heed the voice of their fellow Israelites." (Judges 20:13) Nobody gets handed over. Benjamin comes out of its cities to fight instead.

The answer is that each of them can sling a stone at a hair without missing. The text says each of those 700 left-handers "…could sling a stone at a hair without missing." (Judges 20:16) A hair, friends. I once stamped the same cookie twice, a hair's width off, and called it a design. These men were not doing that.

The answer is that each one is an experienced warrior. The text describes the 400,000 swordsmen as "…each one an experienced warrior." (Judges 20:17) These are not beginners. Keep that in mind, friends, because the numbers look very lopsided on paper.

The answer is False. Israel's huge army does not win easily on the first day. The Benjamites come out of Gibeah and cut down 22,000 Israelites that day (Judges 20:21). All those experienced warriors, and the first day still goes to Benjamin.

The answer is that they're weeping and asking Him what to do. They "…wept before the LORD until evening, inquiring of Him…" about whether to draw near for battle again (Judges 20:23). After losing 22,000 men, they bring their question to Him.

The answer is True. The LORD's answer is "Go up against them." (Judges 20:23) That follows their question about drawing near for battle against their brothers the Benjamites. Hard to hear after a day like that, friends, and I think it was.

The answer is that Benjamin cuts down 18 thousand more. The text says they "…cut down another 18,000 Israelites, all of them armed with swords." (Judges 20:25) Add that to the first day's 22,000 and it's a heavy loss. This is the hardest stretch of the story.

The answer is that they fast and present offerings. That day they "…fasted until evening and presented burnt offerings and peace offerings to the LORD." (Judges 20:26) They sat weeping, fasted and brought offerings. All of it is before Him.

The answer is True. They ask, "Should we again go out to battle against our brothers the Benjamites, or should we stop?" (Judges 20:28) That's a new part of the question. After two days like that, friends, I think stopping was on the table.

The answer is that He'll deliver Benjamin into their hand tomorrow. The LORD answers, "Fight, for tomorrow I will deliver them into your hand." (Judges 20:28) Two hard days, then a promise with a day attached. Tomorrow is the day.

The answer is that Benjamin attacks just as before. The Benjamites came out against Israel and "…began to attack the people as before…" (Judges 20:31) They were drawn away from the city as they did it. It looks like the same story as days one and two.

The answer is True. That's the plan. The Israelites say, "Let us retreat and draw them away from the city onto the roads." (Judges 20:32) Meanwhile the Benjamites are saying they're winning as before. Israel's retreat is part of the plan, friends.

The answer is False. The text says plainly, "But the Benjamites did not realize that disaster was upon them." (Judges 20:34) The battle is fierce, and they still can't see it coming. They only realize later.

The answer is the LORD. The text says, "The LORD defeated Benjamin in the presence of Israel…" (Judges 20:35) Israel had an ambush and big numbers, and the text still names Him. It matches the promise from the day before (Judges 20:28).

The answer is their whole city burning. The Benjamites look behind them and see "…the whole city going up in smoke." (Judges 20:40) That column of smoke was the signal Israel had set up (Judges 20:38). Everything changes in that moment.

The answer is True. The men of Israel turned back on them, and "…the men of Benjamin were terrified when they realized that disaster had come upon them." (Judges 20:41) Earlier the Benjamites had said, "They are defeated before us as in the first battle." (Judges 20:39)

The answer is False. The text says they fled toward the wilderness, "…but the battle overtook them…" (Judges 20:42) They can't get away from it. Israel surrounds and pursues them, and overtakes them easily near Gibeah (Judges 20:43).
The answer is the rock of Rimmon. The text says the 600 "…turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon…" (Judges 20:47) That's the place the text names.

The answer is months. The 600 stayed there four months (Judges 20:47). That's a long stretch to stay in one spot, friends. The text only says they stayed, and I won't guess what those months were like.

The answer is that they're burned down. The text says the men of Israel "…burned down all the cities in their path." (Judges 20:48) Along with that, they put the cities to the sword, including the animals and everything else they found. This is a heavy ending to the passage.
